content.title: What are equals() and hashCode()?
content.description: equals() and hashCode() are two important methods of the Object class. They are used to compare objects and support efficient storage and retrieval in hash-based collections such as HashMap and HashSet.

content.content: The equals() method checks whether two objects are logically equal, while the hashCode() method returns an integer hash value for an object. These two methods work together and must follow a specific contract to ensure collections behave correctly.

content.title: Why Are They Important?
content.content: Without correctly overriding equals() and hashCode(), collections like HashMap and HashSet may store duplicate objects or fail to retrieve existing ones.
The equals() method determines whether two objects should be considered logically equal. By default, Object compares memory references, but most classes override it to compare object data.

content.title: Default equals() Behavior

content.content: Custom classes typically override equals() so that objects with the same data are treated as equal instead of comparing memory locations.

content.title: equals() Example
Key Idea
content.description: equals() compares object contents, not memory addresses, when it is properly overridden.

content.content: The hashCode() method generates an integer value representing an object. Java collections use this value to quickly locate objects in hash-based data structures.

content.title: Hash-Based Collections
content.content: HashMap, HashSet, Hashtable, and LinkedHashMap all depend on hashCode() for efficient searching and storage.
Whenever equals() is overridden, hashCode() should also be overridden. Objects that are equal must always return the same hash code.

items.answer: Stores and retrieves key-value pairs efficiently.

items.question: LinkedHashMap
items.answer: Maintains insertion order while using hashing.

items.question: Caching Systems
items.answer: Efficient object lookup depends on proper hashing.

content.title: Library Books
content.content: A library first uses the shelf number (hashCode) to locate a section quickly and then checks the book title and author (equals) to find the exact book. Java collections follow the same approach.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Questions about equals(), hashCode(), their contract, HashMap internals, HashSet behavior, and the difference between equals() and == are extremely common in Java interviews.

items.question: Can equals() be overridden without hashCode()?
items.answer: Technically yes, but it breaks the contract and causes incorrect behavior in hash-based collections.

items.question: Does the same hash code always mean objects are equal?
items.answer: No. Different objects can produce the same hash code (hash collision).

content.title: Remember This
content.description: equals() checks logical equality, while hashCode() supports efficient searching. Always override both methods together when defining object equality.
